newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Guam seeks more fuel oil, less diesel in 1997-98.
newsitem.headline: Guam seeks more fuel oil, less diesel in 1997-98.

text.p: Guam Power Authority (GPA) is expected to import more fuel oil and less diesel in 1997-1998, a GPA official said on Tuesday.

Randy Wegan, GPA's general manager, said fuel oil demand for August 1997-July 1998 is expected to rise to 3.3 million barrels, compared with about 2.4-2.5 million barrels during the same period in 1996-1997.
About three million barrels required for the next import period are for 2.0-percent sulphur fuel oil, and around 300,000 barrels for the 1.19-percent sulphur grade, Wegan told Reuters by telephone.

GPA currently has an annual term contract with Daxin Petroleum Pte Ltd for deliveries between August 1 1996 and July 31 1997. GPA's previous contract for April 1995-March 1996 was with Vitol Asia Pte Ltd.
Wegan said fuel oil demand for the current period was lower because two of its four fuel oil-fired baseload power generators have been down for maintenance.
One of the generators resumed operations in June while the other is due to restart on November 15.
Due to these shutdowns, GPA was forced to run its smaller fast-track generators which are diesel-fired at full steam, he said.
This forced up its diesel demand to 40 million gallons (1.27 million barrels) in 1996-1997, he said.
But with the baseload generators expected to be running normally next year, diesel demand is expected to pare down to around 30 million gallons (952,380 barrels) in 1997-1998, he said.
GPA currently has three purchase contracts for 0.5-percent sulphur diesel with the local affiliate of Shell and two with the Mobil affiliate to meet its 40-million-gallon demand, he said.
Wegan said GPA has the option to renew its fuel oil and diesel contracts with the existing suppliers for 1997-1998.
But it could also reissue import tenders during end-April for fuel oil and end June for diesel, he added.
